title: Heisenberg scaling under collective non-parallel directional noise via geometric state design
authors: Francisco Riberi, Milad Marvian, Lorenza Viola
abstract: Spin-squeezed states enable entanglement-enhanced frequency estimation; however, the achievable performance is limited in practice by decoherence. We study the problem of parameter estimation under \emph{classical collective noise} that acts along a \emph{fixed} direction during signal encoding. While we restrict our analysis to Gaussian noise statistics, no assumption is made on the nature of the noise temporal correlations. Our approach captures both parallel (dephasing) and single-axis transverse noise as special cases, and covers both Markovian and non-Markovian metrological regimes. In the properly squeezed limit, where a Holstein-Primakoff description is accurate, we identify a geometric noise-immunity mechanism: for \emph{known} non-parallel signal and noise axes, an appropriate one-axis-twisted input encodes the signal in a quadrature that is metric-orthogonal to the direction of noise-induced diffusion. Irrespective of the noise temporal correlations, the resulting estimation precision exhibits Heisenberg scaling in the probe number. Optimal performance is achievable by measuring a single collective spin component. Imperfect knowledge of the noise axis produces a crossover from Heisenberg scaling at moderate probe number back to the known collective-dephasing bounds asymptotically.
summary: The paper develops a theory showing how to maintain Heisenberg scaling in quantum frequency estimation despite classical directional noise. This immunity is achieved by engineering the initial quantum state such that the signal encoding direction is geometrically orthogonal to the noise diffusion direction. The results confirm this robustness, while also quantifying the performance degradation when the noise environment is only partially known.
main_problem: The core problem is achieving Heisenberg scaling ($\Delta\hat{b} \propto N^{-1}$) in quantum parameter estimation when the system is subjected to classical collective directional noise, especially when the signal and noise axes are non-parallel.
main_result: A geometric noise-immunity mechanism was identified: by designing an appropriate input state (One-Axis-Twisted State), the signal encoding can be made metric-orthogonal to the noise diffusion direction, preserving Heisenberg scaling regardless of noise temporal correlations.
method: The analysis uses the Holstein-Primakoff approximation to map the spin system to bosonic quadratures and employs the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) derived from the Wigner function evolution under noise averaging.
model_or_system: The model involves an ensemble of N effective two-level systems whose collective spin operators $\mathbf{J}$ are used to estimate a static frequency $b$. The noise is modeled as classical, Gaussian, and acting along a fixed direction $\hat{\mathbf{v}}$.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), estimation uncertainty ($\Delta\hat{b}$), Wigner function ($W(x, p)$), and the optimal measurement quadrature.
important_parameters: Probe number $N$, noise correlation time $	au$ (governing Markovian/non-Markovian regimes), signal axis angle $	heta$, and noise direction $\hat{\mathbf{v}}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Holstein-Primakoff approximation for tractability, assuming Gaussian statistics for the noise, and analyzing small deviations from perfect knowledge of the noise axis.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates geometric protection by showing how optimal state design keeps the QCRB insensitive to noise diffusion. Figure 2 demonstrates that Heisenberg scaling is maintained for all noise correlation types when full noise knowledge is assumed, but degrades if the noise axis is imperfectly known.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of directional noise limiting metrology. It then introduces the geometric immunity mechanism using OATS states to achieve metric-orthogonality between signal and noise directions. Finally, it analyzes the breakdown of this scaling when the noise direction knowledge becomes imperfect.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, physically realizable protocol for enhancing quantum sensing beyond the Standard Quantum Limit by actively designing input states that are robust against specific types of environmental noise, which is highly relevant to trapped-ion and cavity QED platforms.
